messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

Here's a draft. You didn't say which service or platform, so I've left bracketed placeholders — swap them and it's ready to send.

---

**Subject: [Service] is moving to [new platform] in [Q_]**

Hi [name],

We're moving [Service] to [new platform] next quarter. Here's what that means for you.

The move happens on [date]. [Service] will be unavailable from [start time] to [end time] that day while we transfer accounts and data. Everything you have with us — [projects, saved settings, billing history] — comes across. You don't need to export anything or re-enter payment details.

Two things do change. First, the address: after the move, sign in at [new URL] instead of [old URL]. We'll redirect the old address for [six months], but update your bookmarks and anything pointing at [old API endpoint]. Second, [change #2 — e.g. API v1 retires on <date>; v2 docs are here: <link>].

Why we're doing it: [one honest sentence — e.g. the current platform can't hold the uptime we've promised you, and working around that has been eating time we'd rather spend on <thing customers want>].

What we need from you before [date]:

- [action 1]
- [action 2]

We'll email a reminder a week out, and again the morning of. Live status during the move will be at [status page].

If this timing is a problem for your team, reply to this email and we'll sort something out. [Name] and I are watching the inbox.

[Signature]

---

Two notes on choices I made: the "why" line is worth keeping honest rather than upbeat — customers read around vagueness there. And if there's no real customer action required, cut that list instead of padding it.
